required_fixes: Candidate 4 leaves out the existing v1 boundary that decides who gets tenant-managed credentials. TenantSecrets resolves `tenant.<id>.<field>` references only when the collection is `prisma-airs-scm` (src/api_client/scm/mod.rs:27,169,215). Every other collection falls through to the API Client's own secret namespace. That collection identity is read from the collection file itself (crates/rusty-core/src/project/discovery.rs:61, workflow.rs:210). A search found the identity only at its constant definition, and no reservation of it, so the research should establish whether a user-authored or imported collection can claim it. The built-in SCM collection is also an ordinary, user-editable collection whose edits are kept (scm/mod.rs:10-12,352). Its OAuth `token_url` and request URLs are document variables (scm/mod.rs:321-325). As a result: (a) 'Real variation: managed tenant credentials versus workbench-owned credentials' and 'built-in SCM and user/imported requests obey the same policy' misstate the v1 baseline. In v1, ordinary user/imported collections do not receive tenant credentials. (b) An edited built-in request or token URL can send tenant client secrets to any destination that Network::Live admits. Record this as observed reference. State whether v2 keeps, reserves or replaces collection-identity scoping (a selected-design question; no interface is needed). Add test cases for an imported collection that declares the SCM identity and for an edited token_url/request URL. Fingerprint discovery.rs and workflow.rs.

optional_suggestions: Assessment of attempt-01's ten required fixes. Resolved: (1) automatic 401 resend, accurately described from session/worker/execution.rs:231-273 and backed by C15:30 'no automatic replay'; (2) redactions-based redirect and Live destination policy, matching execution.rs:29-31 and 221-237, with active<4 at worker/execution.rs:107-110; (3) the 81-entry SCM catalogue, with a count of 81 confirmed and catalog.json/ui/api_client/request.rs now fingerprinted; (4) editor truth through ADR 1/24/27; (5) request::Client credential lookup at request.rs:345-358 and the preserved Admission rules, consistent with request.rs:633-673 and ADR 16; (7) the native engine's Node/airs-cli assumptions (runtime_bundle.rs:43,54-78; connection.rs:772-785; airs_desktop_runtime.rs:104,242-244); (8) signature/JWKS checks labelled as a stricter v2 requirement, consistent with ADR 30:57-62; (9) hosted theme coupling (use-theme-preference.ts:17-26, shell/index.ts:9-13, package.json deps); (10) other priorities given an explicit disposition. Partly resolved: (6) file hashes (see required fixes).

The HTML authority 'Before' diagram still puts 'Worker process | credential lookup' in the red leakage box. This contradicts the corrected text, which says credential lookup is already GPUI-free in request::Client. Relabel it as, for example, 'Worker process (Node bridge)'.

Editor-truth nuance: ADR 24 rejected the 'one step owning draft text' option because of keystroke lag and two sources of truth. It explicitly kept 'module-owned draft values, editors as a mirror' as a possible later step (0024:153-159). Saying ADR 24 'rejected module-owned editable text' slightly overstates this.

The Admission summary could also keep the read priority tiers (Visible, then Startup(rank), then Background) and the rule that a read's deadline starts at its permit, so a queued read cannot time out (ADR 16:47-55).

Candidate 3 could note that Academy device authorization also runs through a bundled Node worker (academy.rs:82-106, academy-worker.js). It could also note that the v1 manifest requires package.json (runtime_bundle.rs:78) besides bin/node and managed-cli/airs-cli.
Candidate 3 could note that ADR 31 records workspace MCP as verified only with fakes and a literal runtime (0031:3,129). Retained MCP behaviour is therefore fixture-level evidence.

Candidate 4: a cross-origin managed redirect calls attempt.stop(), which returns the 3xx response rather than an error. Same-origin 307/308 redirects keep method and body. Wording such as 'stops following' is more precise than 'blocks'.
